title: Revelation 9 — The fifth and sixth trumpets: the star, the abyss, the locusts + the horsemen from the Euphrates

translation.sourceText: Koine Greek New Testament — SBL Greek New Testament (SBLGNT), ed. Michael W. Holmes (Society of Biblical Literature and Logos Bible Software, 2010), printed text with the variant-marker sigla removed. Primary uncial witnesses for Revelation: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01) and Codex Alexandrinus (A/02), with Ephraemi Rescriptus (C/04) and P47/P115 where extant; Codex Vaticanus (B/03) does not contain Revelation in its original hand. Variants against NA28 and the Byzantine/Textus Receptus tradition are reported in the verse commentary (overlay convention sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-revelation).

verdicts.reasoning: astera ek tou ouranou peptōkota eis tēn gēn (perfect participle: 'that had fallen'); hē kleis tou phreatos tēs abyssou 'the key of the pit of the abyss' (ASV). The canon's English quotes KJV 'bottomless pit'; its French 'le puits de l'abîme' matches the line. Reception note verified; no leakage.
ēnoixen to phrear tēs abyssou ... hōs kapnos kaminou megalēs ... eskotōthē ho hēlios kai ho aēr. Exact.
edothē autais exousia hōs echousin exousian hoi skorpioi tēs gēs: 'power' for the natural capacity compared to scorpions is defensible (ASV, RSV) and governed by the overlay exousia rule.
errethē autais hina mē adikēsousin (future) ... ei mē tous anthrōpous hoitines ouk echousi tēn sphragida tou theou. 'but only those people' renders ei mē. Exact.

edothē autois (masc. by sense) hina mē apokteinōsin autous, all' hina basanisthēsontai mēnas pente. Exact. Reception note (aircraft, radiation) verified and confined to the labelled paragraph; the line keeps 'locusts', 'scorpion'.
zētēsousin ... ou mē heurēsousin ... pheugei (present) ho thanatos. The tense shift is kept. Exact.
ta homoiōmata tōn akridōn homoia hippois ...; hōs stephanoi homoioi chrysō 'what seemed crowns like gold'. Every comparison marker preserved.
trichas hōs trichas gynaikōn; hoi odontes autōn hōs leontōn ēsan. Exact.

thōrakas hōs thōrakas sidērous: 'breastplates' (all major versions) with the anatomical sense recorded in commentary; the canon's French 'thorax' reading stays in the reception note. Disputed only against the canon's French; the conventional rendering is the defensible one. No leakage.
echousin ouras homoias skorpiois kai kentra, kai en tais ourais autōn hē exousia autōn adikēsai: 'power' located in the tails, per the overlay rule; agrees with ASV, RSV and the canon's English.
basilea ton angelon tēs abyssou; onoma autō Hebraisti Abaddōn, kai en tē Hellēnikē onoma echei Apollyōn. Both names transliterated as in all versions; Apollo wordplay correctly hedged ('possibly').
Hē ouai hē mia apēlthen; idou erchetai eti dyo ouai. 'first' for mia and the singular verb noted. Exact.

citations: Metzger, A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament (2nd ed. 1994), on Rev 9:13
verdicts.reasoning: phōnēn mian ek tōn keratōn tou thysiastēriou tou chrysou tou enōpion tou theou: SBLGNT omits tessarōn and the line follows. The SBLGNT marker confirms an edition reads the word (Robinson-Pierpont at least), consistent with the Editor's corrected attribution (P47, A, Sinaiticus corrector omit; Sinaiticus first hand and Byzantine include) and with Metzger's 'evenly balanced' and NA28's brackets. Reviewer could not check the printed NA28 apparatus in this session; the corrected attribution agrees with the reviewer's reading of Metzger, and a founder spot-check is optional. theos 'God' against the canon's English 'Yahweh' is correct. Reception note (loudspeakers) verified; no leakage.
legonta tō hektō angelō, ho echōn tēn salpinga: nominative solecism noted; Lyson ... epi tō potamō tō megalō Euphratē. Exact.
hoi hētoimasmenoi eis tēn hōran kai hēmeran kai mēna kai eniauton: one article over four nouns, one appointed moment, as the note says. Exact.
dismyriades myriadōn 'twice ten thousand times ten thousand' (ASV); ēkousa ton arithmon autōn. Exact.

thōrakas pyrinous kai hyakinthinous kai theiōdeis; ek tōn stomatōn ... pyr kai kapnos kai theion. 'sulfur' (NRSV; LXX equivalent of gophrit) for KJV/ASV 'brimstone' is lexically exact; 'of hyacinth' keeps the 21:20 link. 'in the vision' as the book's sole horasis correctly noted.

apo tōn triōn plēgōn toutōn apektanthēsan to triton tōn anthrōpōn, ek tou pyros kai tou kapnou kai tou theiou. Exact; 'sulfur' per gophrit extension. Reception note (jet engines, warheads) verified; the line renders kephalai/ourai in their ordinary sense.
hē gar exousia tōn hippōn en tō stomati autōn estin kai en tais ourais autōn: 'power' per the overlay rule (RSV/NRSV). Exact.

oude metenoēsan ek tōn ergōn tōn cheirōn autōn, hina mē proskynēsousin ta daimonia kai ta eidōla ... 'so as not to worship' renders the result/purpose hina with future. Defensible (ASV 'that they should not worship').
phonōn ... pharmakōn ... porneias ... klemmatōn. 'sorceries', 'fornication' (ASV) defensible; the idolatry metaphor is the stated reason for 'fornication' over 'sexual immorality'.

glossaryReview.reasoning: Direct is correct for a presentation and scope convention. Recommendation (non-blocking): state the scope criterion explicitly. Hebrew-text central entries are applied to a Greek line when their English choice is also a correct rendering of the Greek lexeme (chayyot 'living creatures' at 7:11; gophrit 'sulfur' for theion). They are background only where applying them would import a Hebrew-specific form or sense (Yisra'el, 'the adversary', 'the deep'). Without that sentence the 7:11 chayyot ref and the gophrit extension look like exceptions to rule (4).

Direct is defensible: the ASV structure keeps phrear as a separate noun, the Second Temple sense of abyssos (place of confinement) is correctly distinguished from LXX təhôm, and the canon's French 'puits de l'abîme' matches.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Every English line was checked: all 146 lines, and specifically the 21 reception-note sites (7:3, 8:1, 8:7, 8:8, 8:10, 8:12, 9:1, 9:5, 9:9, 9:13, 9:18, 10:4, 10:7, 12:12, 13:18, 16:18, 16:20, 16:21, 21:1, 21:2, 21:3). A script found no Elohim, Yahweh, YHWH, craft, missile, atomic, nuclear, planet, Eternals, loudspeaker or similar lens vocabulary in any line. The only hits were 'ship(s)' (8:9 ploia; worship) and 'Israel' (substring 'rael'), both benign. Each Wheel of Heaven reading sits in its own headed paragraph labelled 'reception note, not a translation claim'. Each was verified against LWTE ch. 2 (LWTE-2:155-228), FR and EN. No line resolves an ambiguity in the canon's direction: the visionary hōs/homoios markers are kept (8:8; 9:7-10), 'the number of a man' stays open (13:18), 'breastplates' is used rather than the canon's French 'thorax' (9:9), 'pit of the abyss' is kept (9:1), and theos is 'God' where the canon's English has 'Yahweh'/'Elohim' (9:13; 21:2-4). Where the line and the canon's English diverge, the line follows the Greek critical text, and at 8:7 that text agrees with the canon's French.

founderDecisionRecommendations.B-theos-God-not-Yahweh-Elohim: Endorse firmly. theos does not render the Tetragrammaton, the canon's own French has 'Dieu', and chapters 1, 4, 6 are signed off with 'God'. Writing 'Yahweh' would translate the canon's English edition, not the Greek.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-critical-text-over-KJV-wording: Endorse. Optionally name 16:3 zōsa and 21:4 hoti.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὁ πέμπτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ εἶδον ἀστέρα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πεπτωκότα εἰς τὴν γῆν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἡ κλεὶς τοῦ φρέατος τῆς ἀβύσσου·
paragraphs.translit: kai ho pemptos angelos esalpisen· kai eidon astera ek tou ouranou peptōkota eis tēn gēn, kai edothē autō hē kleis tou phreatos tēs abyssou·

i18n.en: And the fifth angel sounded, and I saw a star that had fallen from heaven to the earth, and the key of the pit of the abyss was given to him.

notes.official:
*astera ek tou ouranou peptōkota eis tēn gēn* 'a star that had fallen from heaven to the earth': the perfect participle shows the star already fallen when John sees it, and it is treated as a person ('the key ... was given to him'), as stars are angels at 1:20 and in 1 En 86-88. *hē kleis tou phreatos tēs abyssou* 'the key of the pit of the abyss'. *phrear* is a well or shaft; *hē abyssos* 'the abyss' is in Revelation the prison of hostile powers (9:11; 11:7; 17:8; 20:1-3; cf. Luke 8:31; 1 En 18:11-16; 21:7-10). The Septuagint uses *abyssos* for Heb. *təhôm* 'the deep' (Gen 1:2), but here the word names a place of confinement, not the cosmic waters, so the central `tehom` ('the deep') is background only. The line keeps 'pit' and 'abyss' (ASV; `abyssos-pit-of-the-abyss-rendering-revelation`); the KJV 'bottomless pit' renders the etymology of *a-byssos* 'without bottom'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 2) quotes vv 1-2 (English edition 'the bottomless pit', after the KJV; French 'le puits de l'abîme') and reads them as the description of a missile falling and the mushroom cloud it produces. The line keeps 'star', 'pit' and 'abyss' and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἤνοιξεν τὸ φρέαρ τῆς ἀβύσσου, καὶ ἀνέβη καπνὸς ἐκ τοῦ φρέατος ὡς καπνὸς καμίνου μεγάλης, καὶ ἐσκοτώθη ὁ ἥλιος καὶ ὁ ἀὴρ ἐκ τοῦ καπνοῦ τοῦ φρέατος.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēnoixen to phrear tēs abyssou, kai anebē kapnos ek tou phreatos hōs kapnos kaminou megalēs, kai eskotōthē ho hēlios kai ho aēr ek tou kapnou tou phreatos.

i18n.en: And he opened the pit of the abyss, and smoke went up out of the pit like the smoke of a great furnace, and the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke of the pit.

notes.official: *hōs kapnos kaminou megalēs* 'like the smoke of a great furnace': the smoke of Sodom (Gen 19:28) and of Sinai (Ex 19:18) 'went up as the smoke of a furnace'. *ho aēr* 'the air' is the lower atmosphere. 'Pit' and 'abyss' as in v 1 (`abyssos-pit-of-the-abyss-rendering-revelation`).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐκ τοῦ καπνοῦ ἐξῆλθον ἀκρίδες εἰς τὴν γῆν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐταῖς ἐξουσία ὡς ἔχουσιν ἐξουσίαν οἱ σκορπίοι τῆς γῆς.
paragraphs.translit: kai ek tou kapnou exēlthon akrides eis tēn gēn, kai edothē autais exousia hōs echousin exousian hoi skorpioi tēs gēs.

i18n.en: And out of the smoke came locusts upon the earth, and power was given to them, as the scorpions of the earth have power.

notes.official: *akrides* 'locusts': the eighth Egyptian plague (Ex 10:12-15) as transformed by Joel 1-2, whose locust army has 'the appearance of horses' (Joel 2:4). *edothē autais exousia* 'power was given to them': the passive *edothē* 'was given' marks each destructive force in the book as permitted (6:2, 4, 8; 13:5, 7). *exousia* means both the right to act (authority) and the capacity to act (power) (BDAG). The overlay rule `exousia-authority-power-rendering-revelation` uses 'authority' where *exousia* is jurisdiction conferred over persons or things (6:8; 12:10; 13:2-12; 16:9) and 'power' where it is an animal's natural capacity to injure, compared here to scorpions and located in tails and mouths at 9:10, 19 (so RSV, and NRSV at 9:10, 19). *dynamis* is always 'power'.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐρρέθη αὐταῖς ἵνα μὴ ἀδικήσουσιν τὸν χόρτον τῆς γῆς οὐδὲ πᾶν χλωρὸν οὐδὲ πᾶν δένδρον, εἰ μὴ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους οἵτινες οὐκ ἔχουσι τὴν σφραγῖδα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων.
paragraphs.translit: kai errethē autais hina mē adikēsousin ton chorton tēs gēs oude pan chlōron oude pan dendron, ei mē tous anthrōpous hoitines ouk echousi tēn sphragida tou theou epi tōn metōpōn.

i18n.en: And they were told not to harm the grass of the earth or any green thing or any tree, but only those people who do not have the seal of God on their foreheads.

notes.official: *errethē autais hina mē adikēsousin* 'they were told not to harm' (*hina* with the future indicative). Unlike the locusts of Exodus and Joel, these may not touch vegetation; they are sent against 'those people who do not have the seal of God on their foreheads', referring back to 7:3. *pan chlōron* 'any green thing'.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ ἀποκτείνωσιν αὐτούς, ἀλλʼ ἵνα βασανισθήσονται μῆνας πέντε· καὶ ὁ βασανισμὸς αὐτῶν ὡς βασανισμὸς σκορπίου, ὅταν παίσῃ ἄνθρωπον.
paragraphs.translit: kai edothē autois hina mē apokteinōsin autous, allʼ hina basanisthēsontai mēnas pente· kai ho basanismos autōn hōs basanismos skorpiou, hotan paisē anthrōpon.

i18n.en: And it was given to them not to kill them, but that they should be tormented five months; and their torment was like the torment of a scorpion when it strikes a man.

notes.official:
*edothē autois hina mē apokteinōsin autous* 'it was given to them not to kill them': the masculine *autois* refers to the locusts by sense (the noun *akrides* is feminine). *basanisthēsontai* 'they should be tormented'. *mēnas pente* 'five months' is often explained as the life span of a locust (Charles, ICC; Aune, WBC 52B). *hotan paisē anthrōpon* 'when it strikes a man'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 2) quotes vv 5-6 (English edition 'they were not given authority to kill them') and reads the locusts as aircraft loaded with atomic bombs, and the scorpion's sting as the suffering inflicted by radiation on those who survive the explosions. The line renders the zoological terms in their ordinary sense and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ζητήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι τὸν θάνατον καὶ οὐ μὴ εὑρήσουσιν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐπιθυμήσουσιν ἀποθανεῖν καὶ φεύγει ὁ θάνατος ἀπʼ αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai en tais hēmerais ekeinais zētēsousin hoi anthrōpoi ton thanaton kai ou mē heurēsousin auton, kai epithymēsousin apothanein kai pheugei ho thanatos apʼ autōn.

i18n.en: And in those days people will seek death and will by no means find it; and they will long to die, and death flees from them.

notes.official: *zētēsousin ... kai ou mē heurēsousin* 'will seek ... and will by no means find': the emphatic negation *ou mē*. *pheugei* 'flees' is a present after a series of futures (ASV 'fleeth'), and the change of tense is kept. Cf. Job 3:21; Jer 8:3.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ τὰ ὁμοιώματα τῶν ἀκρίδων ὅμοια ἵπποις ἡτοιμασμένοις εἰς πόλεμον, καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν ὡς στέφανοι ὅμοιοι χρυσῷ, καὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὡς πρόσωπα ἀνθρώπων,
paragraphs.translit: kai ta homoiōmata tōn akridōn homoia hippois hētoimasmenois eis polemon, kai epi tas kephalas autōn hōs stephanoi homoioi chrysō, kai ta prosōpa autōn hōs prosōpa anthrōpōn,

i18n.en: And the shapes of the locusts were like horses prepared for war; and on their heads were what seemed crowns like gold, and their faces were like the faces of men,

notes.official: *ta homoiōmata tōn akridōn homoia hippois* 'the shapes of the locusts were like horses': from Joel 2:4. The repeated *hōs* and *homoios* ('like', 'what seemed') mark every feature in vv 7-10 as a comparison. *prosōpa anthrōpōn* 'the faces of men'.

paragraphs.text: καὶ εἶχον τρίχας ὡς τρίχας γυναικῶν, καὶ οἱ ὀδόντες αὐτῶν ὡς λεόντων ἦσαν,
paragraphs.translit: kai eichon trichas hōs trichas gynaikōn, kai hoi odontes autōn hōs leontōn ēsan,

i18n.en: and they had hair like the hair of women, and their teeth were like lions' teeth,

notes.official: *trichas hōs trichas gynaikōn* 'hair like the hair of women'; *hoi odontes autōn hōs leontōn* 'their teeth were like lions' teeth', from Joel 1:6 ('its teeth are the teeth of a lion').

paragraphs.text: καὶ εἶχον θώρακας ὡς θώρακας σιδηροῦς, καὶ ἡ φωνὴ τῶν πτερύγων αὐτῶν ὡς φωνὴ ἁρμάτων ἵππων πολλῶν τρεχόντων εἰς πόλεμον·
paragraphs.translit: kai eichon thōrakas hōs thōrakas sidērous, kai hē phōnē tōn pterygōn autōn hōs phōnē harmatōn hippōn pollōn trechontōn eis polemon·

i18n.en: and they had breastplates like breastplates of iron, and the sound of their wings was like the sound of chariots, of many horses running into war;

notes.official:
*thōrakas hōs thōrakas sidērous* 'breastplates like breastplates of iron'. *thōrax* means both the chest and the armour that covers it, the cuirass (LSJ; BDAG). The military sense suits horses 'prepared for war' (v 7) and 'running into war', and every major version has 'breastplates'; the anatomical sense is also present, since a locust's thorax is plated. *hē phōnē tōn pterygōn autōn hōs phōnē harmatōn hippōn pollōn* 'the sound of their wings was like the sound of chariots, of many horses': Joel 2:5 ('like the noise of chariots').

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 2) quotes vv 9-10. Its French reads *thōrax* in the anatomical sense ('des thorax comme des thorax de fer') and explains the iron thorax as the fuselage of an aircraft, the noise as that of jet engines, the 'teeth' as missiles under the wings, the women's hair as condensation trails, and the power in the tails as radiation; its English edition has 'breastplates'. The line keeps the conventional 'breastplates' and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἔχουσιν οὐρὰς ὁμοίας σκορπίοις καὶ κέντρα, καὶ ἐν ταῖς οὐραῖς αὐτῶν ἡ ἐξουσία αὐτῶν ἀδικῆσαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους μῆνας πέντε.
paragraphs.translit: kai echousin ouras homoias skorpiois kai kentra, kai en tais ourais autōn hē exousia autōn adikēsai tous anthrōpous mēnas pente.

i18n.en: and they have tails like scorpions, and stings, and in their tails is their power to harm people for five months.

notes.official: *kentra* 'stings'. *en tais ourais autōn hē exousia autōn adikēsai tous anthrōpous* 'in their tails is their power to harm people': 'power', as the bodily location shows the capacity to harm (`exousia-authority-power-rendering-revelation`; see 9:3); the ASV and the canon's English edition ('their power was to hurt men') agree. *echousin* 'they have' is a descriptive present.

paragraphs.text: ἔχουσιν ἐπʼ αὐτῶν βασιλέα τὸν ἄγγελον τῆς ἀβύσσου· ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ἑβραϊστὶ Ἀβαδδών, καὶ ἐν τῇ Ἑλληνικῇ ὄνομα ἔχει Ἀπολλύων.
paragraphs.translit: echousin epʼ autōn basilea ton angelon tēs abyssou· onoma autō hebraisti abaddōn, kai en tē hellēnikē onoma echei apollyōn.

i18n.en: They have as king over them the angel of the abyss; his name in Hebrew is Abaddon, and in Greek he has the name Apollyon.

notes.official: *echousin ep' autōn basilea* 'They have as king over them': contrast Prov 30:27, 'the locusts have no king'. *ton angelon tēs abyssou* 'the angel of the abyss' (`abyssos-pit-of-the-abyss-rendering-revelation`). *Abaddōn* transliterates Heb. *ʾăbaddôn* 'destruction', the place of the dead paired with Sheol (Job 26:6; 28:22; Prov 15:11; Ps 88:12). *Apollyōn* 'Destroyer' is a participial name from *apollymi*, possibly also a play on Apollo, one of whose emblems was the locust (Aune, WBC 52B; Koester, AB 38A). *Hebraisti* 'in Hebrew' (cf. 16:16). Both names stay transliterated, as in all major versions (`greek-nt-proper-names-and-hebrew-scoped-entries-convention-revelation`).

paragraphs.text: Ἡ οὐαὶ ἡ μία ἀπῆλθεν· ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται ἔτι δύο οὐαὶ μετὰ ταῦτα.
paragraphs.translit: hē ouai hē mia apēlthen· idou erchetai eti dyo ouai meta tauta.

i18n.en: The first woe has passed; behold, two woes are still to come after these things.

notes.official: *Hē ouai hē mia* 'The first woe': *ouai* is treated as a feminine noun, and *mia* 'one' stands for 'first', a Semitic usage (cf. Gen 1:5). *erchetai eti dyo ouai* 'two woes are still to come' has a singular verb with a plural subject.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὁ ἕκτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν μίαν ἐκ τῶν κεράτων τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τοῦ χρυσοῦ τοῦ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: kai ho hektos angelos esalpisen· kai ēkousa phōnēn mian ek tōn keratōn tou thysiastēriou tou chrysou tou enōpion tou theou,

i18n.en: And the sixth angel sounded, and I heard a voice from the horns of the golden altar that is before God,

notes.official:
*phōnēn mian ek tōn keratōn tou thysiastēriou tou chrysou* 'a voice from the horns of the golden altar'. The word *tessarōn* 'four' before *keratōn* is read by the first hand of Sinaiticus and the Byzantine text (KJV 'the four horns') and is absent from P47, Alexandrinus and the corrector of Sinaiticus. The evidence is evenly balanced, and NA28 prints the word in brackets (Metzger, *Textual Commentary*², ad loc.). The SBLGNT omits it, and the line follows (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-revelation`). The incense altar had four horns at its corners (Ex 30:2-3; central `qarnot-ha-mizbeach-horns-of-the-altar-cross-corpus`, literal 'the horns of the altar'), so the number is implied either way. *mian* 'one' is rendered as the indefinite 'a', as at 8:13. This is the altar from which the prayers of the saints rose (8:3-5).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 2) quotes this verse with 'the four horns' (French 'des quatre cornes') and, in its English edition, 'before Yahweh' (French 'devant Dieu'). It reads the four horns as four loudspeakers placed in front of the speaker while he showed John these scenes. The line translates the SBLGNT, renders *theos* 'God' (`theos-god-rendering-against-canon-english-yahweh-revelation`) and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: λέγοντα τῷ ἕκτῳ ἀγγέλῳ, ὁ ἔχων τὴν σάλπιγγα· Λῦσον τοὺς τέσσαρας ἀγγέλους τοὺς δεδεμένους ἐπὶ τῷ ποταμῷ τῷ μεγάλῳ Εὐφράτῃ.
paragraphs.translit: legonta tō hektō angelō, ho echōn tēn salpinga· lyson tous tessaras angelous tous dedemenous epi tō potamō tō megalō euphratē.

i18n.en: saying to the sixth angel, the one who had the trumpet: "Release the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates."

notes.official: *legonta tō hektō angelō, ho echōn tēn salpinga* 'saying to the sixth angel, the one who had the trumpet': the nominative *ho echōn* in apposition to a dative is another of the book's solecisms (cf. 1:5). *epi tō potamō tō megalō Euphratē* 'at the great river Euphrates': the ideal eastern boundary of the promised land (Gen 15:18; Deut 1:7) and, in the first century, the frontier with Parthia. Angels bound and then released recall the bound Watchers of 1 En 10:4-12, and 1 En 56:5-8 has angels stir up the Parthians and Medes from the east.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐλύθησαν οἱ τέσσαρες ἄγγελοι οἱ ἡτοιμασμένοι εἰς τὴν ὥραν καὶ ἡμέραν καὶ μῆνα καὶ ἐνιαυτόν, ἵνα ἀποκτείνωσιν τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
paragraphs.translit: kai elythēsan hoi tessares angeloi hoi hētoimasmenoi eis tēn hōran kai hēmeran kai mēna kai eniauton, hina apokteinōsin to triton tōn anthrōpōn.

i18n.en: And the four angels were released, who had been prepared for the hour and day and month and year, to kill a third of mankind.

notes.official: *hoi hētoimasmenoi eis tēn hōran kai hēmeran kai mēna kai eniauton* 'who had been prepared for the hour and day and month and year': a single article governs the four nouns, so one appointed moment is meant, not a period of a year, a month, a day and an hour. *to triton tōn anthrōpōn* 'a third of mankind'.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν στρατευμάτων τοῦ ἱππικοῦ δισμυριάδες μυριάδων· ἤκουσα τὸν ἀριθμὸν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho arithmos tōn strateumatōn tou hippikou dismyriades myriadōn· ēkousa ton arithmon autōn.

i18n.en: And the number of the troops of cavalry was twice ten thousand times ten thousand; I heard their number.

notes.official: *dismyriades myriadōn* 'twice ten thousand times ten thousand', i.e. 200,000,000 (cf. Ps 68:17; Dan 7:10). *tou hippikou* 'of cavalry'. *ēkousa ton arithmon autōn* 'I heard their number', as with the sealed in 7:4.

paragraphs.text: καὶ οὕτως εἶδον τοὺς ἵππους ἐν τῇ ὁράσει καὶ τοὺς καθημένους ἐπʼ αὐτῶν, ἔχοντας θώρακας πυρίνους καὶ ὑακινθίνους καὶ θειώδεις· καὶ αἱ κεφαλαὶ τῶν ἵππων ὡς κεφαλαὶ λεόντων, καὶ ἐκ τῶν στομάτων αὐτῶν ἐκπορεύεται πῦρ καὶ καπνὸς καὶ θεῖον.
paragraphs.translit: kai houtōs eidon tous hippous en tē horasei kai tous kathēmenous epʼ autōn, echontas thōrakas pyrinous kai hyakinthinous kai theiōdeis· kai hai kephalai tōn hippōn hōs kephalai leontōn, kai ek tōn stomatōn autōn ekporeuetai pyr kai kapnos kai theion.

i18n.en: And thus I saw the horses in the vision and those seated on them: they had breastplates of fire and of hyacinth and of sulfur; and the heads of the horses were like the heads of lions, and out of their mouths come fire and smoke and sulfur.

notes.official: *en tē horasei* 'in the vision': the only use of the word in the book, which marks the scene explicitly as a vision. *thōrakas pyrinous kai hyakinthinous kai theiōdeis* 'breastplates of fire and of hyacinth and of sulfur': colour adjectives, fire-red, dark blue (*hyakinthinos*, the colour of the hyacinth flower or the jacinth stone; `foundation-stones-gem-names-rev-21-19-20`) and sulfur-yellow. The three colours match the 'fire and smoke and sulfur' that come out of the horses' mouths. *theion* 'sulfur' (KJV, ASV 'brimstone') follows the central `gophrit-va-esh-destruction-formula`: the Septuagint renders Heb. *gop̄rîṯ* by *theion* (Gen 19:24), and the entry's own treatment of the Revelation reception renders *theion* 'sulfur'. The decision is here extended to the Greek text. *ekporeuetai* 'come out' is present.

paragraphs.text: ἀπὸ τῶν τριῶν πληγῶν τούτων ἀπεκτάνθησαν τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἐκ τοῦ πυρὸς καὶ τοῦ καπνοῦ καὶ τοῦ θείου τοῦ ἐκπορευομένου ἐκ τῶν στομάτων αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: apo tōn triōn plēgōn toutōn apektanthēsan to triton tōn anthrōpōn, ek tou pyros kai tou kapnou kai tou theiou tou ekporeuomenou ek tōn stomatōn autōn.

i18n.en: By these three plagues a third of mankind was killed, by the fire and the smoke and the sulfur coming out of their mouths.

notes.official:
*apo tōn triōn plēgōn toutōn* 'By these three plagues', i.e. the fire, the smoke and the sulfur. *apektanthēsan to triton tōn anthrōpōn* 'a third of mankind was killed': plural verb, construction according to sense. *theion* 'sulfur' (`gophrit-va-esh-destruction-formula`; see v 17).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 2) quotes vv 18-19 (English edition 'brimstone', after the KJV) and reads the heads of the horses as jet engines emitting flames and smoke, and the tails 'that had heads' as nuclear missiles with their warheads. The line renders *theion* 'sulfur', *kephalai* 'heads' and *ourai* 'tails' in their ordinary sense and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: ἡ γὰρ ἐξουσία τῶν ἵππων ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτῶν ἐστιν καὶ ἐν ταῖς οὐραῖς αὐτῶν· αἱ γὰρ οὐραὶ αὐτῶν ὅμοιαι ὄφεσιν, ἔχουσαι κεφαλάς, καὶ ἐν αὐταῖς ἀδικοῦσιν.
paragraphs.translit: hē gar exousia tōn hippōn en tō stomati autōn estin kai en tais ourais autōn· hai gar ourai autōn homoiai ophesin, echousai kephalas, kai en autais adikousin.

i18n.en: For the power of the horses is in their mouth and in their tails; for their tails are like serpents, having heads, and with them they do harm.

notes.official: *hē gar exousia tōn hippōn en tō stomati autōn estin* 'For the power of the horses is in their mouth': singular *stoma* used distributively; 'power' as at v 10 (`exousia-authority-power-rendering-revelation`). *hai gar ourai autōn homoiai ophesin, echousai kephalas* 'for their tails are like serpents, having heads'. *adikousin* 'they do harm'.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, οἳ οὐκ ἀπεκτάνθησαν ἐν ταῖς πληγαῖς ταύταις, οὐδὲ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν, ἵνα μὴ προσκυνήσουσιν τὰ δαιμόνια καὶ τὰ εἴδωλα τὰ χρυσᾶ καὶ τὰ ἀργυρᾶ καὶ τὰ χαλκᾶ καὶ τὰ λίθινα καὶ τὰ ξύλινα, ἃ οὔτε βλέπειν δύνανται οὔτε ἀκούειν οὔτε περιπατεῖν,
paragraphs.translit: kai hoi loipoi tōn anthrōpōn, hoi ouk apektanthēsan en tais plēgais tautais, oude metenoēsan ek tōn ergōn tōn cheirōn autōn, hina mē proskynēsousin ta daimonia kai ta eidōla ta chrysa kai ta argyra kai ta chalka kai ta lithina kai ta xylina, ha oute blepein dynantai oute akouein oute peripatein,

i18n.en: And the rest of mankind, who were not killed by these plagues, did not repent of the works of their hands, so as not to worship demons and idols of gold and of silver and of bronze and of stone and of wood, which can neither see nor hear nor walk;

notes.official: *hoi loipoi tōn anthrōpōn* 'the rest of mankind'. *oude metenoēsan ek tōn ergōn tōn cheirōn autōn* 'did not repent of the works of their hands': 'the work of their hands' means idols in prophetic polemic (Deut 4:28; Jer 1:16). *hina mē proskynēsousin* 'so as not to worship' (*hina* with the future). The materials and the idols 'which can neither see nor hear nor walk' come from Dan 5:4, 23 and Ps 115:4-7 (113:12-15 LXX). *ta daimonia* 'demons': the identification of idols with demons comes from Deut 32:17 and Ps 96:5 LXX (95:5); cf. 1 Cor 10:20.

paragraphs.text: καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν φόνων αὐτῶν οὔτε ἐκ τῶν φαρμάκων αὐτῶν οὔτε ἐκ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῶν οὔτε ἐκ τῶν κλεμμάτων αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ou metenoēsan ek tōn phonōn autōn oute ek tōn pharmakōn autōn oute ek tēs porneias autōn oute ek tōn klemmatōn autōn.

i18n.en: and they did not repent of their murders, nor of their sorceries, nor of their fornication, nor of their thefts.

notes.official: The list of murders, sorceries, fornication and thefts follows the second table of the Decalogue (Ex 20:13-15). *pharmakōn* 'sorceries' covers drugs, spells and poisons (BDAG). *porneia* is 'fornication' (ASV), as in the central `apostolic-decree-acts-15-noahide-leviticus-17-18-cross-corpus` (Acts 15:29) and at 21:8 'fornicators'. In Revelation the word also carries the prophetic metaphor of idolatry as unfaithfulness (Hos 4:12; Rev 14:8; 17:2), which 'fornication' keeps better than 'sexual immorality'.
